draft.title: Calmer rhythm lights: minimum gap, weak-hit threshold and bar-to-bar smoothing (#43)
draft.context: Rhythm lights play `Groove.pattern`: each sixteenth's level is (v − typical)/(loudest − typical), multiplied by `playing` (how hard the kicks hit now compared with usual). Nothing spaces the pulses, so syncopated kicks flash every ~86 ms at 174 BPM. Any sixteenth above the typical one lights, including ghost notes and bass lines. `playing` follows a fast average of recent kicks, so the strength jumps from bar to bar. The tracker already takes up live settings: `BeatTracking.listen` reads `TrackerSettings.from(live.applied)` on every hop. The pattern can therefore be calmed where it's built, with the bpm and settings at hand.
draft.decision:
Calm the pattern inside the beat tracker, so `AudioReading.groove` keeps its meaning and `Effects`, `Pulse` and `SyncEngine` don't change. The new `RhythmSettings(minGapMs, threshold, smoothing)` sits under `ReactiveSettings.rhythm` and reaches the tracker through `TrackerSettings.rhythm`. `BeatTracker.reading` emits `groove.calm(settings.rhythm, beat.bpm)` instead of `groove.pattern`. While fewer than 16 sixteenths are learnt, `calm` returns `Groove.Prior` unchanged.

`calm` works in three pure steps, in the new `beat.Calm`:
1. Threshold: each level v becomes 0 if v ≤ t, else (v − t)/(1 − t). The loudest sixteenth stays 1, and t = 0 is the identity.
2. Strength: multiply by the smoothed strength `Groove.strength`, not by `playing`.
3. Gap: d = the smallest whole number of sixteenths with d × 15000/bpm ≥ minGapMs. If d ≤ 1 the pattern is unchanged. Otherwise the lit sixteenths are grouped greedily around the bar, starting at the first lit sixteenth after the longest unlit run. A group's pulse sits on its first sixteenth, at the group's strongest value, and the rest are zeroed. If the bar's last group starts less than d before the next bar's first pulse, it merges into the group before it. With d = 2 from about 94 BPM up, 160 ms keeps 174 BPM eighths (172 ms) apart.

Smoothing is a slew limit applied to `strength` each time a sixteenth is learnt (`Calm.follow`):
- With s = 0, the strength equals `playing`.
- Otherwise it moves towards `playing` by at most 0.08 × (1 − s)/s per bar. At the default 0.5 that's 8% a bar, which keeps bar-to-bar jitter under 10% whatever the noise. An EMA only does that on average.
- A drop-out (`playing` < 0.4) or a return (strength < 0.4) skips the slew limit and takes `playing` straight away, so returning kicks show at once.
- While s > 0, a strength under 0.15 shows as rest. That puts lights at rest within 4 bars of a drop-out, and back above half within 1–2 bars of a return.

At 0/0/0, each step is the identity, so `calm` equals `pattern` exactly.
draft.components:
- `model`: new `RhythmSettings`, `ReactiveSettings.rhythm`, and three range checks in `LightShowConfig.problems`.
- `root`: a `ConfigReader[RhythmSettings]` given, and a `rhythm {}` block in reference.conf.
- `beat`: `TrackerSettings.rhythm`, filled by `from(show)`. `Groove` gains `strength`, `levels`, `playing` and `calm`, and `at` takes `smoothing` (default 0). `BeatTracker.step` passes `s.rhythm.smoothing` to `at`, and `reading` calls `calm`. New `Calm` holds the pure maths.
- `ui`: three sliders in `Sections.rhythmAndPulse`, through a `rhythm` change helper.
- Calls: Settings page → LiveSettings → `TrackerSettings.from` → BeatTracker → Groove → Calm → AudioReading.groove → Effects/Pulse (unchanged).
draft.contracts:
- Config keys (additive, with defaults): `light-show.reactive.rhythm.min-gap-ms` (Long, 160), `.threshold` (Double, 0.3), `.smoothing` (Double, 0.5).
- Shared model (additive): `RhythmSettings` in `model`, compiled for the JVM and JS; `ReactiveSettings.rhythm: RhythmSettings = RhythmSettings()`, the last parameter.
- Settings JSON: `reactive.rhythm {minGapMs, threshold, smoothing}`. The derived circe codec makes it required on POST. That's safe because the page and the server ship together and the page sends the full object it was given. `ConfigSnippet` lists the field as `reactive.rhythm.min-gap-ms` etc. without changes.
- `TrackerSettings.rhythm: RhythmSettings = RhythmSettings()` (additive).
- `Groove`: `strength: Double = 0.0` is added last; `at(beats, kick, smoothing = 0.0)` keeps every caller compiling; `pattern` is unchanged.
- `AudioReading.groove` keeps its type and meaning: the pattern the rhythm lights play.
- No new environment variables or HTTP endpoints.
draft.failureModes:
- Config boundary: a value out of range is fatal at startup. `LightShowConfig.problems` adds one problem per setting:
  - "reactive.rhythm.min-gap-ms must be between 0 and 400"
  - "reactive.rhythm.threshold must be between 0 and 0.9"
  - "reactive.rhythm.smoothing must be between 0 and 0.9"

  The existing pureconfig `CannotConvert` reports them, and the settings page's update rejects the same list, so a bad save is recoverable.
- Engine: `Calm` is total. A threshold ≤ 0.9 means 1 − t > 0. If bpm ≤ 0 (which the tracker never gives), the gap is 1 sixteenth, meaning no spacing. There is no new runtime boundary, so no new error type; validation keeps its existing `List[String]`.
draft.config: reference.conf gets, under `reactive`, a commented `rhythm { min-gap-ms = 160, threshold = 0.3, smoothing = 0.5 }`. The case class defaults match, so leaving out the block or any key gives the defaults. The ranges are checked at startup in `LightShowConfig.problems` (min-gap-ms 0–400, threshold 0–0.9, smoothing 0–0.9, all inclusive), and the app refuses to start on a bad value. The UI sliders use steps of 10, 0.05 and 0.05.
draft.observability: No new log lines. Nothing new crosses a boundary or fails at runtime, and logging per frame or per sixteenth would flood the log. Startup and save failures already name the bad key through the existing problems message. The settings page's config snippet shows any of the three settings that are off their defaults.
alternatives: Apply the settings in `Effects.at` and keep the smoothing state in the render loop's `RenderState`. That widens `AudioReading` with raw levels and playing, and puts music state into the pause-fade renderer. The tracker already has live settings and per-sixteenth state.

Keep a per-bar history of `playing` in `Groove` and filter it when the pattern is read. It needs a weighting by position in the bar to avoid a jump at each bar line, so it's more code for the same result.
Smooth with an EMA (retain s per bar) instead of a slew limit. An EMA only meets the 10% bar-to-bar bound on average: at s = 0.5 with ±20% loudness it exceeds 10% on roughly one bar in seven.

skeleton.content:
package domain.config

import io.circe.Codec

/**
 * How calmly the rhythm lights follow the kick pattern. Kicks closer together than `minGapMs` merge into one pulse on
 * the first kick's sixteenth, as strong as the strongest. A sixteenth lights only once it stands out by `threshold` of
 * the gap between the bar's typical and loudest sixteenth. `smoothing` slows how far the pattern's overall strength can
 * move from one bar to the next. 0 switches each one off.
 */
case class RhythmSettings(
  minGapMs: Long = 160,
  threshold: Double = 0.3,
  smoothing: Double = 0.5
) derives Codec.AsObject

package domain.config

import domain.engine.LightRole
import io.circe.Codec

/**
 * How the show reacts to live audio, beyond the beat.
 *
 * Each light gets a job from `roles`, repeated across the zone in channel order. Rhythm lights pulse with the bar's
 * kick pattern, calmed by `rhythm`. Colour lights swell with `colourSwell`, once every couple of beats, and move up to `colourReach` palette
 * colours along the palette as the music goes higher or lower. Pulse lights do the classic travelling pulse, their palette turning by up to `colourShift`
 * degrees as the treble picks up or drops away.
 *
 * Brightness follows the music's energy, between `quietest` and `loudest` times normal. A big hit (louder than
 * anything in the last few seconds by `hitRatio`) flashes every light towards white by `flash`, fading over
 * `flashDecayMs`; a treble onset (`sparkleRatio` times the usual background) twinkles one light that isn't a rhythm
 * light by `sparkle`, fading over `sparkleDecayMs`.
 */
case class ReactiveSettings(
  enabled: Boolean = true,
  quietest: Double = 0.35,
  loudest: Double = 1.6,
  colourShift: Double = 25.0,
  flash: Double = 0.7,
  flashDecayMs: Long = 200,
  hitRatio: Double = 1.15,
  sparkle: Double = 0.6,
  sparkleDecayMs: Long = 100,
  sparkleRatio: Double = 4.0,
  roles: List[LightRole] = List(LightRole.Rhythm, LightRole.Colour),
  colourReach: Double = 1.0,
  colourSwell: SwellSettings = SwellSettings(),
  rhythm: RhythmSettings = RhythmSettings()
) derives Codec.AsObject

package beat

import domain.config.{LightShowConfig, RhythmSettings}
import scala.concurrent.duration.*

case class TrackerSettings(
  sampleRate: Double = 44100,
  hop: Int = 512,
  window: Int = 1024,
  historySeconds: Double = 8.0,
  minBpm: Double = 60,
  maxBpm: Double = 180,
  reestimateEvery: Int = 22,
  silenceRms: Double = 0.002,
  minConfidence: Double = 2.5,
  keepConfidence: Double = 1.2,
  steadySeconds: Double = 3.0,
  phaseSwitch: Double = 0.6,
  phaseMemorySeconds: Double = 10.0,
  holdSeconds: Double = 10.0,
  hitRatio: Double = 1.15,
  sparkleRatio: Double = 4.0,
  rhythm: RhythmSettings = RhythmSettings()
) {
  val frameRate: Double = sampleRate / hop
  val hopDuration: FiniteDuration = (hop / sampleRate).seconds.toNanos.nanos
  val capacity: Int = (historySeconds * frameRate).toInt
  val minFrames: Int = (4.0 * frameRate).toInt
  val hitWindow: Int = (4.0 * frameRate).toInt
  val sparkleWindow: Int = (2.0 * frameRate).toInt
  val steadyEstimates: Int = math.max(1, (steadySeconds * frameRate / reestimateEvery).round.toInt)

  /** Smoothing factor of an exponential average with the given time constant, per hop. */
  def smoothing(seconds: Double): Double = 1 - math.exp(-(hop / sampleRate) / seconds)
}

object TrackerSettings {

  /** The tracker's tuning, from the light show's settings. */
  def from(show: LightShowConfig): TrackerSettings =
    TrackerSettings(
      minBpm = show.audio.minBpm,
      maxBpm = show.audio.maxBpm,
      holdSeconds = show.audio.holdSeconds,
      hitRatio = show.reactive.hitRatio,
      sparkleRatio = show.reactive.sparkleRatio,
      rhythm = show.reactive.rhythm
    )
}

slices.title: Calmer rhythm lights: min-gap-ms, threshold and smoothing
slices.delivers: The three rhythm settings, end to end: config, validation, settings JSON, the tracker's calmed pattern, the settings page sliders and the docs.
acceptanceCriteria: On generated audio with kicks a sixteenth apart above 94 BPM, at the default minimum gap no two rhythm-light peaks are less than 160 ms apart, including across the bar line. Each group of close kicks gives one pulse, on its first kick's sixteenth, at the strength of its strongest kick
On generated 174 BPM drum-and-bass audio with kicks an eighth apart, at the default minimum gap each kick gets its own rhythm-light pulse
On generated audio with a steady kick plus a bass line at half the kick's power in 40–130 Hz, on the 'and' of each beat and the last sixteenth, only the kick sixteenths pulse at the default threshold
At threshold t, a sixteenth at level v > t lights at (v − t)/(1 − t), one at or below t is dark, and the loudest sixteenth is still 1

On generated audio with steady kicks whose loudness varies at random by ±20% from bar to bar, at the default smoothing the rhythm pattern's peak changes by no more than 10% of the peak between consecutive bars
When the kick drops out, at the default smoothing the rhythm pattern is all zero within 4 bars. When it returns, its peak is at least 0.5 within 2 bars
With minimum gap 0, threshold 0 and smoothing 0, the rhythm pattern equals today's `Groove.pattern` exactly on the same audio
With no rhythm settings configured, the loaded config has minimum gap 160 ms, threshold 0.3 and smoothing 0.5
A config with min-gap-ms outside 0–400, threshold outside 0–0.9 or smoothing outside 0–0.9 fails to load, with a message naming that setting. The settings page rejects the same values

The settings page's 'Rhythm and pulse lights' section shows sliders for reactive.rhythm.min-gap-ms (0–400, step 10), reactive.rhythm.threshold (0–0.9, step 0.05) and reactive.rhythm.smoothing (0–0.9, step 0.05). Saving them changes the settings the tracker uses

docs/how-it-works.md's rhythm lights section explains the minimum gap, threshold and smoothing. Its config table lists reactive.rhythm.min-gap-ms (0–400, 160), reactive.rhythm.threshold (0–0.9, 0.3) and reactive.rhythm.smoothing (0–0.9, 0.5). reference.conf comments the new block
slices.testStrategy:
CalmSpec (pure):
- Tables: `gapSteps` at 60/94/120/174/180 BPM; `spaced` for adjacent pairs, wrap-around at the bar line, all sixteenths lit, and gap 1 as the identity.
- Properties: `threshold` gives 0 at t and below, 1 at 1, and is monotone in between; `spaced` output is never closer than the gap, cyclically, and keeps each group's maximum on its first sixteenth; `follow` with smoothing 0 returns `playing`, otherwise moves at most StepPerBar·(1 − s)/s per 16 calls unless crossing DropOut.

GrooveSpec:
- Property: `calm` at 0/0/0 equals `pattern` on random kick streams.
- Property: `calm` returns `Prior` before a bar is learnt.

BeatTrackerSpec, on Synth-generated audio:
- syncopated sixteenths at 120/140 BPM;
- 174 BPM eighths;
- kick plus a half-power bass line;
- ±20% bar loudness from a seeded Random;
- a drop-out and return.

Each asserts on `reading.groove` per bar. Each fails on master, where `pattern` is played. Nothing is wall-clock timed; Synth timestamps the frames.

LightShowConfigSpec: a table of in-range and out-of-range values for each key, plus the defaults when the block is missing.

SettingsJsonSpec: round-trip with `rhythm`.

SectionsSpec (Node): slider ranges and steps, and that `set` updates `reactive.rhythm` and `TrackerSettings.from` picks it up.

```scala
package beat

import domain.config.RhythmSettings

/** Calms the kick pattern for the rhythm lights: weak sixteenths dropped, close kicks merged, strength steadied. */
object Calm {

  /** Below this strength the kicks have dropped out, and the smoothed strength follows them at once. */
  val DropOut: Double = 0.4

  /** While smoothing, a strength below this shows as rest. */
  val Resting: Double = 0.15

  /** How far the strength may move in a bar at smoothing 0.5; it scales with (1 - s) / s. */
  val StepPerBar: Double = 0.08

  /** The pattern to play: `levels` thresholded, scaled by `strength` and spaced at least `minGapMs` apart at `bpm`. */
  def pattern(levels: Vector[Double], strength: Double, settings: RhythmSettings, bpm: Double): Vector[Double] = ???

  /** 0 up to `t`, then rising to 1 at the loudest: (v - t) / (1 - t). */
  def threshold(level: Double, t: Double): Double = ???

  /** The fewest sixteenths at `bpm` that are at least `minGapMs` long; at least 1. */
  def gapSteps(minGapMs: Long, bpm: Double): Int = ???

  /**
   * Lit sixteenths fewer than `gap` apart, around the bar, merged into one on the group's first, as strong as its
   * strongest. Grouping starts after the longest unlit run; a last group too close to the bar's first joins the one before.
   */
  def spaced(pattern: Vector[Double], gap: Int): Vector[Double] = ???

  /** The strength after one more sixteenth heard, moving towards `playing` no faster than `smoothing` allows. */
  def follow(strength: Double, playing: Double, smoothing: Double): Double = ???

  /** The strength the lights show: rest below [[Resting]] while smoothing. */
  def shown(strength: Double, smoothing: Double): Double = ???
}
```

findings.headline: Smoothing the pattern can't stop the lights flickering, because loudness still moves their brightness
findings.ifIgnored: Criterion 5 is signed off on a pattern test while the real rhythm-light peaks still swing by about 20% from bar to bar.
findings.section: Slices — criterion 5 and the BeatTrackerSpec ±20% test
findings.problem: Criterion 5 is about the rhythm lights' peak brightness. The slice quietly turns it into "the rhythm pattern's peak" and tests only `reading.groove`. Rhythm-light brightness is `Pulse.brightness(level, …, effects.intensity)`, and `Effects.at` sets intensity from `reading.energy` (`loudNow/loudUsual`, which tracks "a second or two", about one bar at 120 BPM). With bar loudness varying at random by ±20%, intensity varies by close to that from bar to bar, so peak brightness changes by much more than 10% even when the pattern's strength is perfectly steady.
findings.suggestion: Measure criterion 5 on rendered rhythm-light brightness, for example in a SyncEngine or Effects test fed by the tracker. Then either take the rhythm lights' share of intensity out of bar-to-bar loudness, or show that intensity is clamped or slow enough at the defaults. Don't narrow the criterion's wording in the slice.

findings.headline: Settings-page test plans to use a tracker type the browser build can't see
findings.ifIgnored: The slice doesn't compile under `sbt check`. If the line is dropped instead, nothing tests that saving the sliders changes the tracker.
findings.problem: SectionsSpec runs under Scala.js in Node, but it is meant to check that `TrackerSettings.from` picks up `reactive.rhythm`. `TrackerSettings` is in `src/main/scala/beat`, the JVM-only server module, so the UI test can't reference it. The second half of criterion 10 ("saving them changes how the rhythm lights behave") then has no test that can actually run.
findings.suggestion: Keep the slider ranges, steps and `set` checks in the Node SectionsSpec. Add a JVM test that applies a settings update through LiveSettings, or the settings endpoint, and asserts that `TrackerSettings.from(applied).rhythm`, or the tracker's reading, reflects it.

findings.headline: The bass-line test likely already passes on master, so it proves nothing
findings.ifIgnored: Criterion 3 gets a test that doesn't fail without the change, against the issue's explicit requirement, and threshold behaviour isn't shown on real audio.
findings.section: Slices — BeatTrackerSpec "kick plus a half-power bass line"
findings.problem: With kicks on 4 sixteenths, bass on 5 (the "and" of each beat plus the last sixteenth) and 7 empty, the sorted shape is 7 zeros, then 5 bass values, then 4 kicks. `pattern` takes the typical level from `sorted(8)`, which is a bass value, so on master the bass sixteenths already come out at level 0 and only the kicks pulse. The design says every BeatTrackerSpec case "fails on master" but doesn't show it for this one, and the arithmetic says it won't.
findings.suggestion: Check the Synth output on master before relying on it. If master passes, keep the issue's audio and assert something that does change. For example, assert that the bass sixteenths' levels before thresholding fall between typical and loudest and are dark only after the threshold. Or add bass bleed onto the empty sixteenths so the typical level drops below the bass. Then say in the design why the test fails on master.

findings.headline: Gap tests on kick patterns with 8+ equal sixteenths will see all-dark lights
findings.ifIgnored: The gap tests may pass on master too, and the 174 BPM test may fail after the change for a reason unrelated to the gap.
findings.section: Slices — BeatTrackerSpec syncopated and 174 BPM eighths tests; CalmSpec "all sixteenths lit"
findings.problem: `pattern` (and `levels`) compares each sixteenth with `sorted(8)`. If 8 or more of the 16 sixteenths carry an equal kick, the typical level equals the loudest, the gap between them is 0, and the whole pattern is zero. Kicks a sixteenth apart on every beat (0,1 / 4,5 / …), or kicks on every eighth at 174 BPM, both give 8 kick sixteenths. The 160 ms check then passes trivially on master, and criterion 2 ("each kick gets its own pulse") fails after the change. The CalmSpec "all sixteenths lit" case can't come from real audio either.
findings.suggestion: Pin the generated patterns in the design to 7 kick sixteenths or fewer per bar. For example, use pairs a sixteenth apart on two beats, and DnB kicks at 0 and 2, then 10. Assert that the lights are lit, i.e. some peak above 0.5, before checking the spacing.

findings.headline: Pulses are spaced only within one snapshot, so peaks can still come too close
findings.ifIgnored: Criterion 1 is tested on static snapshots, so real playback can still flash twice within 160 ms when the pattern's state shifts.
findings.section: Decision — Gap step; Slices — "asserts on reading.groove per bar"
findings.problem: `spaced` groups the lit sixteenths of one pattern, starting after the longest unlit run. The pattern is rebuilt every hop: a sixteenth near the threshold can flick on or off, the longest unlit run can move, and bpm can cross a d boundary. Any of these can move a group's start mid-bar, so the light plays a pulse at sixteenth k and then another at k+1 from the regrouped pattern. Criterion 1 is about peak times, but the tests sample `reading.groove` once per bar and the properties check one pattern at a time.
findings.suggestion: Check criterion 1 on rendered peak times across the whole run, including across the bar line, not on per-bar snapshots. Either show that grouping is stable under those changes, or enforce the gap over time, e.g. remember when the last pulse was played and hold later ones back. Add audio that drifts in tempo or near the threshold to the test.

findings.headline: At high smoothing, lights can stay dim for a minute after a partial dip
findings.ifIgnored: Users who raise the smoothing slider see rhythm lights stuck dim for long stretches after any dip that isn't a full drop-out.
findings.problem: The step per bar is 0.08 × (1 − s)/s, so at s = 0.9 the strength moves about 0.009 a bar. A dip that stays above the 0.4 drop-out cutoff, say to 0.45, takes about 60 bars to recover. Below 0.4 the strength jumps straight to the new level instead. The result is a cliff in behaviour around 0.4 and very slow recovery near the top of the slider's range.
findings.suggestion: Bound the slowest recovery, for example with a floor on the step per bar, or let rises move faster than falls. Document the response time at 0.9.

findings.headline: A setting given as NaN passes the range checks and breaks the lights
findings.ifIgnored: `threshold = NaN` in the config is accepted at startup, and the rhythm lights get NaN brightness.
findings.problem: Range checks written as `x < 0 || x > 0.9` are false for NaN, so `threshold` or `smoothing` set to NaN is accepted. NaN then flows through (v − t)/(1 − t) and the slew limit into the pattern and on to the Hue colours.
findings.suggestion: Write the checks as `!(x >= 0 && x <= 0.9)` so NaN is rejected with the same message.

draft.title: Calmer rhythm lights: minimum gap, weak-hit threshold and bar-to-bar smoothing (#43)
draft.context: Rhythm-light brightness is `(restLevel + peakBoost × Pulse.rhythm(groove, beats)) × intensity`. `groove` is `Groove.pattern`: (v − typical)/(loudest − typical) × `playing`, where typical is `sorted(8)`. `intensity` is `reading.energy`, which follows loudness over about 1.5 s. Three things make the lights erratic: nothing spaces the pulses, any sixteenth above typical lights, and both `playing` and `intensity` jump from bar to bar. The tracker reads live settings on every hop through `TrackerSettings.from(live.applied)`.
draft.decision:
Calm the rhythm lights in the tracker, where the bpm, grid step and per-sixteenth state already are. `Groove` gains a `calm: Calm.State`, updated by a new `at` overload. The pure maths goes in a new `beat.Calm`.
- Threshold: v ≤ t gives 0, otherwise (v − t)/(1 − t). The loudest stays 1, and t = 0 is the identity.
- Gap: d is the fewest sixteenths with d × 15000/bpm ≥ minGapMs. `spaced` merges lit sixteenths fewer than d apart into one pulse on the first, at the group's maximum. `spaced` works on one pattern only, and the pattern is rebuilt every hop, so `held` also enforces the gap over time. `State.lastPulse` is the grid step of the last pulse played. Any slot whose next step falls within d − 1 after it is zeroed, so a regrouped pattern can't add a second peak, across the bar line too. The step is recorded when the grid reaches a lit slot (half a sixteenth early), before the next slot's attack starts.
- Strength: the pattern is scaled by the smoothed `State.strength` instead of `playing`.
- Rhythm intensity: `State.energy` follows `levels.energy` the same way. `AudioReading.rhythmEnergy` carries it, and `Effects.rhythmIntensity` clamps it to quietest–loudest. Only rhythm lights use it. Without this, ±20% bar loudness moves peak brightness by about 15% whatever the pattern does.
- `follow`: each learnt sixteenth moves the value 1/16 of a bar's step towards the target. The step is max(0.02, 0.03 × (1 − s)/s) per bar, but the value never stays more than Jitter = 0.35 from the target.
  - The dead band bounds the slowest recovery. At s = 0.9 a large change closes to within 0.35 at once and finishes at 0.02 a bar, within 18 bars.
  - At the default 0.5, ±20% loudness keeps `playing` (capped at 1) within 0.65–1, so the step applies. Strength moves at most 4.2% of the peak per bar and energy at most 3.8%, under 10% together.
- Drop-out and return: when `playing` or the strength is under 0.4, the strength takes `playing` at once. While s > 0, a strength under 0.15 shows as rest. `recent` halves every bar, so the lights rest by bar 3 and are back above 0.5 within 2 bars.
- At s = 0, strength is `playing` and `rhythmEnergy` is None. With 0/0/0 every step is the identity, so the output equals `pattern` exactly. `Prior` is played unchanged until a bar is learnt.
draft.components:
- `model`: new `RhythmSettings`, `ReactiveSettings.rhythm`, three checks in `LightShowConfig.problems`.
- `root`: a `ConfigReader[RhythmSettings]` given, and a `rhythm {}` block in reference.conf.
- `beat`:
  - `TrackerSettings.rhythm`.
  - New `Calm`.
  - `Groove`: `levels`, `playing`, `calm`, the `at(beats, kick, energy, settings, bpm)` overload, `lights` and `rhythmEnergy`.
  - `BeatTracker.step` calls the overload. `reading` emits `_.lights` and `_.rhythmEnergy`.
- `domain.engine`: `Effects.rhythmIntensity` and `rhythmLight`. `SyncEngine.pulseFrame`'s Rhythm case calls `rhythmLight`.
- `ui`: three sliders in `Sections.rhythmAndPulse`.
- Calls: page → LiveSettings → TrackerSettings.from → BeatTracker → Groove → Calm → AudioReading → Effects → SyncEngine.
draft.contracts:
All changes are additive.
- Config keys: `light-show.reactive.rhythm.min-gap-ms` (Long, 160), `.threshold` (Double, 0.3) and `.smoothing` (Double, 0.5).
- Shared model: `RhythmSettings`, and `ReactiveSettings.rhythm`, added last with a default.
- Settings JSON: `reactive.rhythm {minGapMs, threshold, smoothing}`. The derived codec requires it on POST, which is safe because the page posts back the object it was served. `ConfigSnippet` picks it up as is.
- `AudioReading.rhythmEnergy: Option[Double] = None`, `Effects.rhythmIntensity: Option[Double] = None` and `TrackerSettings.rhythm`, all with defaults.
- `Groove.calm` has a default. The old `at(beats, kick)` and `pattern` are unchanged.
- No environment variables or endpoints change.
draft.failureModes:
- Config: a bad value is fatal at startup through the existing `CannotConvert`. The page's save rejects it through `SettingsProblems`, so a bad save is recoverable. The messages are:
  - "reactive.rhythm.min-gap-ms must be between 0 and 400"
  - "reactive.rhythm.threshold must be between 0 and 0.9"
  - "reactive.rhythm.smoothing must be between 0 and 0.9"
- The Double checks are written `!(x >= 0 && x <= 0.9)`, so NaN is rejected with the same message.
- Engine: `Calm` is total. t ≤ 0.9 keeps 1 − t > 0, and bpm ≤ 0 gives d = 1. There's no new runtime boundary and so no new error type. Validation stays a `List[String]`.
draft.config: reference.conf gets `reactive.rhythm { min-gap-ms = 160, threshold = 0.3, smoothing = 0.5 }`, with comments. The case class defaults match, so a missing block or key gives the defaults. `LightShowConfig.problems` checks the inclusive ranges 0–400, 0–0.9 and 0–0.9 at startup, and the app refuses to start on a bad value. The sliders step by 10, 0.05 and 0.05.
draft.observability: No new log lines. Nothing new fails at runtime, and logging per hop would flood the log. A bad value is already named by the existing startup error and the settings-save problems, and the page's config snippet shows any value off its default.
alternatives: Calm in `Effects`/`RenderState` instead: that needs raw levels in `AudioReading` and puts music state into the pause-fade renderer.

Enforce the gap only by regrouping each pattern: the threshold flicker, the moving unlit run and changes in d all move a group's start between hops, giving a second peak a sixteenth later. `held` closes that.
Smooth with an EMA: it meets the 10% bound only on average, and it recovers geometrically slowly at s = 0.9.

skeleton.content:
package domain.config

import io.circe.Codec

/**
 * How calmly the rhythm lights follow the kick pattern. Kicks closer together than `minGapMs` merge into one pulse on
 * the first kick's sixteenth, as strong as the strongest. A sixteenth lights only once it stands out by `threshold` of
 * the gap between the bar's typical and loudest sixteenth. `smoothing` slows how far the rhythm lights' strength can
 * move from one bar to the next. 0 switches each one off.
 */
case class RhythmSettings(
  minGapMs: Long = 160,
  threshold: Double = 0.3,
  smoothing: Double = 0.5
) derives Codec.AsObject

package domain.config

import domain.engine.LightRole
import io.circe.Codec

/**
 * How the show reacts to live audio, beyond the beat.
 *
 * Each light gets a job from `roles`, repeated across the zone in channel order. Rhythm lights pulse with the bar's
 * kick pattern, calmed by `rhythm`. Colour lights swell with `colourSwell`, once every couple of beats, and move up to `colourReach` palette
 * colours along the palette as the music goes higher or lower. Pulse lights do the classic travelling pulse, their palette turning by up to `colourShift`
 * degrees as the treble picks up or drops away.
 *
 * Brightness follows the music's energy, between `quietest` and `loudest` times normal. A big hit (louder than
 * anything in the last few seconds by `hitRatio`) flashes every light towards white by `flash`, fading over
 * `flashDecayMs`; a treble onset (`sparkleRatio` times the usual background) twinkles one light that isn't a rhythm
 * light by `sparkle`, fading over `sparkleDecayMs`.
 */
case class ReactiveSettings(
  enabled: Boolean = true,
  quietest: Double = 0.35,
  loudest: Double = 1.6,
  colourShift: Double = 25.0,
  flash: Double = 0.7,
  flashDecayMs: Long = 200,
  hitRatio: Double = 1.15,
  sparkle: Double = 0.6,
  sparkleDecayMs: Long = 100,
  sparkleRatio: Double = 4.0,
  roles: List[LightRole] = List(LightRole.Rhythm, LightRole.Colour),
  colourReach: Double = 1.0,
  colourSwell: SwellSettings = SwellSettings(),
  rhythm: RhythmSettings = RhythmSettings()
) derives Codec.AsObject

package beat

import domain.config.{LightShowConfig, RhythmSettings}
import scala.concurrent.duration.*

case class TrackerSettings(
  sampleRate: Double = 44100,
  hop: Int = 512,
  window: Int = 1024,
  historySeconds: Double = 8.0,
  minBpm: Double = 60,
  maxBpm: Double = 180,
  reestimateEvery: Int = 22,
  silenceRms: Double = 0.002,
  minConfidence: Double = 2.5,
  keepConfidence: Double = 1.2,
  steadySeconds: Double = 3.0,
  phaseSwitch: Double = 0.6,
  phaseMemorySeconds: Double = 10.0,
  holdSeconds: Double = 10.0,
  hitRatio: Double = 1.15,
  sparkleRatio: Double = 4.0,
  rhythm: RhythmSettings = RhythmSettings()
) {
  val frameRate: Double = sampleRate / hop
  val hopDuration: FiniteDuration = (hop / sampleRate).seconds.toNanos.nanos
  val capacity: Int = (historySeconds * frameRate).toInt
  val minFrames: Int = (4.0 * frameRate).toInt
  val hitWindow: Int = (4.0 * frameRate).toInt
  val sparkleWindow: Int = (2.0 * frameRate).toInt
  val steadyEstimates: Int = math.max(1, (steadySeconds * frameRate / reestimateEvery).round.toInt)

  /** Smoothing factor of an exponential average with the given time constant, per hop. */
  def smoothing(seconds: Double): Double = 1 - math.exp(-(hop / sampleRate) / seconds)
}

object TrackerSettings {

  /** The tracker's tuning, from the light show's settings. */
  def from(show: LightShowConfig): TrackerSettings =
    TrackerSettings(
      minBpm = show.audio.minBpm,
      maxBpm = show.audio.maxBpm,
      holdSeconds = show.audio.holdSeconds,
      hitRatio = show.reactive.hitRatio,
      sparkleRatio = show.reactive.sparkleRatio,
      rhythm = show.reactive.rhythm
    )
}

package beat

/**
 * What the music is doing right now.
 *
 * `energy` and `treble` compare the last fraction of a second with the track's usual level, so 1.0 means typical,
 * below 1 quieter or duller, above 1 louder or brighter. `hit` is the latest big hit (a crash or a drop), `sparkle`
 * the latest treble onset (hi-hats, cymbals), and `sparkles` counts them, so each can land on a different light.
 * `pitch` is how high the vocals, leads and chords sit compared with usual for the track, from -1 (well below) to 1
 * (well above). `groove` is the pattern the rhythm lights play (see [[Groove.lights]]), empty without a beat. `news` is what the latest hop has to say about how the tempo was chosen.
 * `rhythmEnergy` is `energy` smoothed from bar to bar for the rhythm lights; without it they follow `energy`.
 */
case class AudioReading(
  beat: Option[BeatState],
  energy: Double = 1.0,
  treble: Double = 1.0,
  hit: Option[Hit] = None,
  sparkle: Option[Hit] = None,
  sparkles: Long = 0,
  pitch: Double = 0.0,
  groove: Vector[Double] = Vector.empty,
  news: Vector[TempoNews] = Vector.empty,
  rhythmEnergy: Option[Double] = None
)

slices.title: Calmer rhythm lights: min-gap-ms, threshold and smoothing
slices.delivers: The three rhythm settings end to end: config and validation, settings JSON, the calmed pattern and rhythm intensity, the sliders and the docs.
acceptanceCriteria: On generated audio with kicks a sixteenth apart at a tempo above 94 BPM, at the default minimum gap no two rhythm-light peaks are less than 160 ms apart. Each group of close kicks gives one pulse, on the first kick's sixteenth, at the strength of the group's strongest kick
On generated drum-and-bass audio at 174 BPM with kicks an eighth apart, at the default minimum gap each kick gets its own rhythm-light pulse

On generated audio with a steady kick plus a bass line at half the kick's power in 40–130 Hz, on sixteenths with no kick (the "and" of each beat and the last sixteenth of the bar), only the kick sixteenths pulse at the default threshold

At a threshold of t, a sixteenth that passes the threshold lights in proportion to (v − t)/(1 − t), where v is its level as a fraction of the gap between the bar's typical and loudest sixteenth. The loudest sixteenth in the bar is still full brightness

On generated audio with steady kicks whose loudness varies at random by ±20% from bar to bar, at the default smoothing the rhythm lights' peak brightness changes by no more than 10% of the peak between consecutive bars
When the kick drops out, at the default smoothing the rhythm lights are at rest within 4 bars. When it returns, they reach at least half strength within 2 bars
With minimum gap 0, threshold 0 and smoothing 0, the rhythm lights are exactly as they are today on the same audio
With no rhythm settings configured, the app uses minimum gap 160 ms, threshold 0.3 and smoothing 0.5
If the minimum gap is outside 0–400 ms, the threshold is outside 0–0.9 or the smoothing is outside 0–0.9, the app refuses to start and names the bad setting

The settings page's section for rhythm and pulse lights shows sliders for the minimum gap (0–400 ms, step 10), the threshold (0–0.9, step 0.05) and the smoothing (0–0.9, step 0.05). Saving them changes how the rhythm lights behave

docs/how-it-works.md describes the minimum gap, threshold and smoothing settings in its rhythm lights section, including that at smoothing 0.9 a large change shows at once and the rest catches up within 18 bars. Its config table lists reactive.rhythm.min-gap-ms (0–400, 160), reactive.rhythm.threshold (0–0.9, 0.3) and reactive.rhythm.smoothing (0–0.9, 0.5)
slices.testStrategy:
A new test helper renders the rhythm light on every hop of Synth.readings, as `Effects.at(...).rhythmLight` at the reading's beat count. Peaks are the local maxima of that level above 0.2. A new Synth generator takes per-slot kick and bass powers, a bpm function and per-bar loudness. Every pattern has at most 7 kick sixteenths a bar, because with 8 or more the typical sixteenth equals the loudest and the pattern is all zero.

RhythmLightsSpec (audio through the tracker, Effects and the renderer, all at the defaults; each asserts some peak level > 0.5 before anything else):
- Criterion 1: kicks on {0,1,4,8,9,12} and {0,4,8,9,12,15} (a pair across the bar line), at 120 and 140 BPM, at a tempo drifting 118→126 BPM, and with the pairs' second kicks at random 0.25–0.45 power (near the threshold). Over the whole run no two peaks are less than 160 ms apart. Pair peaks fall within a hop of the first kick's sixteenth. With pair powers (0.7, 1.0), their height matches the single kicks' within 5%. On master, pairs peak a sixteenth (125 ms) apart.
- Criterion 2: 174 BPM with kicks on {0,2,10} and hats on the eighths. Assert the lock is 174 ± 3 BPM, then 3 peaks above 0.5 per bar. This fails before the change because the setting and `rhythmLight` don't exist.
- Criterion 3: kick on the beats, bass on 2/6/10/14/15 at 0.4/0.45/0.5/0.55/0.6 of the kick's power (mean 0.5). On master, typical is the second-quietest bass sixteenth, so three bass sixteenths light at about 0.09–0.27. After the change no bass sixteenth's level tops 0.02.
- Criterion 5: kicks on the beats at 120 BPM, with per-bar loudness from a seeded Random ±20% and hats scaled too. The peak brightness of consecutive bars differs by ≤ 10%. On master both `playing` and `energy` jump, so it fails.
- Criterion 6: 8 bars of kicks, then 6 bars with hats only, then kicks again. The level is 0 from bar 4 of the drop-out, and some peak level is ≥ 0.5 within 2 bars of the return. On master the strength isn't smoothed, so it fails.
- Criterion 7, at 0/0/0 on several Synth runs: `reading.groove` equals `groove.pattern` on every hop, `rhythmEnergy` is None, and the rendered brightness equals today's `Pulse.brightness(Pulse.rhythm(pattern, ...), intensity)`.

CalmSpec (pure):
- Tables: `gapSteps` at 60, 93.75, 94, 120, 174 and 180 BPM, and 0 ms.
- Properties:
  - `threshold` is 0 at and below t, 1 at 1, equal to (v − t)/(1 − t) above t, and the identity at t = 0.
  - `spaced` output is never closer than the gap cyclically, keeps each group's maximum on its first sixteenth, and is the identity at gap 1.
  - Fed any sequence of patterns along an advancing step, `held` never plays two pulses closer than the gap.
  - `follow` returns the target at s = 0. Otherwise it moves at least min(distance, max(0.02, 0.03(1 − s)/s)) and at most that or the excess over Jitter per 16 sixteenths. `strength` takes `playing` below DropOut.

LightShowConfigSpec:
- Defaults when the block is missing.
- A table of in-range, edge and out-of-range values per key, NaN included, each naming its key.

LiveSettingsSpec (JVM): update with new rhythm values, then startSong, then `TrackerSettings.from(applied).rhythm` equals them. A tracker run on the same audio with threshold 0 and with 0.9 gives different `reading.groove`.

SettingsJsonSpec: round-trip with `rhythm`.

SectionsSpec (Node): the three sliders' keys, min, max and step, and that `set` updates `reactive.rhythm`.

```scala
package beat

import domain.config.RhythmSettings

/** Calms the kick pattern for the rhythm lights: weak sixteenths dropped, close kicks merged, strength steadied. */
object Calm {

  /** Below this the kicks have dropped out or are only coming back, and the strength follows them at once. */
  val DropOut: Double = 0.4

  /** While smoothing, a strength below this shows as rest. */
  val Resting: Double = 0.15

  /** How far a smoothed value may move in a bar at smoothing 0.5; it scales with (1 - s) / s. */
  val StepPerBar: Double = 0.03

  /** The least a smoothed value moves in a bar, however high the smoothing, so it always catches up. */
  val MinStepPerBar: Double = 0.02

  /** The furthest a smoothed value stays from what it follows; bar-to-bar jitter is well inside this. */
  val Jitter: Double = 0.35

  /**
   * What the rhythm lights are doing: the kicks' smoothed `strength` and the music's smoothed `energy` (None while
   * not smoothing), the sixteenths `learnt` when they last moved, the grid step of the last pulse played, and the
   * `pattern` being played.
   */
  case class State(
    strength: Double = 0.0,
    energy: Option[Double] = None,
    learnt: Long = 0L,
    lastPulse: Option[Long] = None,
    pattern: Vector[Double] = Vector.empty
  )

  /** `levels` thresholded, scaled by the strength shown and spaced at least `minGapMs` apart at `bpm`. */
  def pattern(levels: Vector[Double], strength: Double, settings: RhythmSettings, bpm: Double): Vector[Double] = ???

  /** 0 up to `t`, then rising to 1 at the loudest: (v - t) / (1 - t). */
  def threshold(level: Double, t: Double): Double = ???

  /** The fewest sixteenths at `bpm` that are at least `minGapMs` long; at least 1. */
  def gapSteps(minGapMs: Long, bpm: Double): Int = ???

  /**
   * Lit sixteenths fewer than `gap` apart, around the bar, merged into one on the group's first, as strong as its
   * strongest. Grouping starts after the longest unlit run; a last group too close to the bar's first joins the one before.
   */
  def spaced(pattern: Vector[Double], gap: Int): Vector[Double] = ???

  /** `pattern` with every slot whose next grid step after `step` is fewer than `gap` after `lastPulse` dark. */
  def held(pattern: Vector[Double], step: Long, lastPulse: Option[Long], gap: Int): Vector[Double] = ???

  /**
   * `current` after `sixteenths` more sixteenths heard, moving towards `target` by at most
   * max([[MinStepPerBar]], [[StepPerBar]] (1 - s) / s) a bar, and never more than [[Jitter]] from it; `target` at s = 0.
   */
  def follow(current: Double, target: Double, smoothing: Double, sixteenths: Long): Double = ???

  /** Like [[follow]], but taking `playing` at once while it or `current` is below [[DropOut]]. */
  def strength(current: Double, playing: Double, smoothing: Double, sixteenths: Long): Double = ???

  /** The strength the lights show: rest below [[Resting]] while smoothing. */
  def shown(strength: Double, smoothing: Double): Double = ???
}
```

findings.headline: Gap check runs on the tracker's clock, but lights are drawn up to 400 ms later in the beat
findings.ifIgnored: At the default 100 ms audio offset, fast tracks can still show a second flash a sixteenth after a merged pulse, which is the strobe the issue is about.
findings.problem: `held` records `lastPulse` and zeroes the next d−1 slots when the tracker's grid, at capture time, reaches a lit slot half a sixteenth early. `SyncEngine.playingFrame` draws the reading at `heardAt = now + audio.offsetMs`, which is 100 ms by default and can be set anywhere from −200 to 400 ms. At 120 BPM, 100 ms is 0.8 of a sixteenth, and at 174 BPM it is more than one (86 ms). By the time the tracker zeroes slot k+1, the renderer has already started k+1's attack, which begins 0.8 of a sixteenth early at attack 0.2, from the previous pattern. So the regrouping double peak that `held` is meant to stop can still show, or a pulse that has started rising gets cut off. The criterion 1 tests draw each reading 'at the reading's beat count', so they never include the offset and can't catch this.
findings.suggestion: Make the hold look ahead by the render offset. One way is to pass `audio.offsetMs` into `TrackerSettings` and run `held` and the `lastPulse` recording at the grid step for `now + offset`. Another is to keep zeroed every slot within d−1 after any lit slot the renderer could already be drawing. Then draw the RhythmLightsSpec peaks at `b.countAt(t + offset)` with the default offset and with the 400 ms maximum, as `playingFrame` does.

findings.headline: If the whole beat drops out, rhythm lights jump back to full pulses on every beat
findings.ifIgnored: In breakdowns with no percussion, rhythm lights reach rest and then go back to full every-beat pulses after about 5 bars, unlike the 'settle to rest' the issue describes.
findings.section: Decision (drop-out and return) and the criterion 6 test
findings.problem: The criterion 6 test keeps hi-hats playing, so the tracker keeps its lock. In a real breakdown with no percussion, the tracker drops the beat once `holdSeconds` (10 s) runs out. `nextGroove` then becomes None and `Effects.rhythm` becomes None, and `pulseFrame` falls back to `Pulse.onBeat` at full strength. When the kick comes back, the new lock plays the Prior at full strength. The calming state is thrown away with the groove, so nothing in the design covers this path.
findings.suggestion: Either add a criterion 6 variant with pads only (no percussion) and decide what rhythm lights do once the beat is lost, or say in the ADR and docs that 'settle to rest' only holds while the beat is held, because losing the beat belongs to the tracker and is out of scope.

findings.headline: When the beat grid jumps backwards, the gap rule could hide every pulse
findings.ifIgnored: After a phase correction, an implementation that follows the spec literally could leave the rhythm lights dark until the grid catches up.
findings.problem: The design notes that the grid can jump, and `Groove.at` already handles steps that don't move forward. `held` zeroes slots whose next step after `step` is 'fewer than gap after lastPulse'. If the beat estimate moves the phase back so that `step < lastPulse`, the difference is negative for every slot, and a plain `next − lastPulse < gap` check would zero the whole pattern. The CalmSpec property only feeds steps that move forward.
findings.suggestion: Specify that `lastPulse` is cleared, or clamped, when `step` goes back past it. Extend the `held` property to sequences of steps that are not monotonic.

findings.headline: Rhythm sliders sit in a section that still says it only shapes pulses
findings.ifIgnored: Users see the calming sliders as active when only pulse lights are assigned, and the section intro doesn't mention them.
findings.problem: The section intro reads 'The shape of each pulse on the rhythm and pulse lights.' Its `unused` check counts the section as in use while any light is a rhythm light or a pulse light. The three new settings only affect rhythm lights, so a zone with pulse lights only shows them enabled even though they change nothing.
findings.suggestion: Update the intro to mention calming the kick pattern. Give the three sliders help text that says they apply to rhythm lights only, or add a per-slider hint about which lights they change.
